paper.title: Pre-symptomatic detection of COVID-19 from smartwatch data
paper.claim: Reproduces the published NightSignal threshold mechanics, limits the Brainstem translation to descriptive overnight heart-rate change from a personal baseline, and separately adds generated-only descriptive movement mechanics.
paper.population: The paper and public sample do not validate a Brainstem device or participant population.
paper.referenceStandard: Pinned author implementation and checksum-pinned compact derivative of its public Fitbit sample.
paper.relationEvidence: The source running-median and two-night +3/+4 bpm mechanics are independently reproduced; the Brainstem seven-prior-night translation and generated movement descriptors are explicitly separate and non-clinical.

compatibility.window: Seven prior qualifying nights followed by two comparison nights.
compatibility.preprocessing: Use compact full-night summaries; calculate the prior-seven median without allowing comparison nights to move their own baseline; derive movement coverage, contiguous events, quiet proportion, and aligned heart-rate means only from the frozen movement contract.
mismatches: The source uses Fitbit/Apple Watch resting heart rate rather than Brainstem R-R-derived sleeping rate.
Source infection labels and alerts are deliberately excluded.
Historical capture-time and device-provenance limitations remain explicit.
Movement descriptors are a generated Brainstem extension and are not part of the NightSignal paper.

cohort.output: Participant-equal aggregate distribution of within-person overnight heart-rate and movement descriptors; no nightly, raw-stream, or disease-labelled rows.

personal.output: Owner-only nine-night heart-rate and movement history with descriptive coverage and within-person change, with non-clinical limitations.
